title: Human targeted sequencing — Ion Torrent public input
finding: This human amplicon run adds targeted sequencing on a semiconductor instrument. It differs from whole-genome sequencing in what is sampled and from the Illumina/MGI inputs in technology. Its amount is close to the middle of 133 comparable runs from the same study.
limit: The inspected source identifies a cfDNA amplicon run, but does not establish exact panel extent or the relation between supplied and integrated reads. No general panel-depth certification is claimed.

title: Spruce target capture public input
finding: This spruce library represents population genotyping by target capture. Its 335 million reported bases are small relative to the proposed 11.96-billion-base spruce reference. That contrast is worth testing for reference-based compression, but no effect has been measured. The archive groups three submitted lane pairs into the two listed FASTQ ends.
limit: The source grouping is metadata evidence, not body-level merge or order verification. Exact normalized representation and library-specific usable target depth remain unverified. Probe count is not a target-base denominator; the earlier cohort’s 15× is not assigned to this run.

title: Quinoa reduced-representation genotyping public input
finding: This RAD library represents crop genotyping from selected parts of a genome. Its amount is close to the middle of 136 comparable study runs. A whole-genome-sized file would describe a different task, so this complete paired run is an appropriate small input.
limit: Do not assess RAD using whole-genome depth. Exact locus coverage is not established by these raw totals.

title: Pig genome with supplied constant qualities public input
finding: This pig genomic run covers livestock sequencing and a file in which the inspected qualities are constant. Those qualities are part of the bytes to preserve. Their origin is unknown, so they are not described as typical native MGI quality output.
limit: The original role is an assembly/resequencing study component. The supplied constant qualities must not be advertised as typical native MGI qualities; their processing origin is unknown.

title: Mouse genome sequencing public input
finding: This mouse tail-DNA run adds a commonly used research animal and its genome reference. It is one complete germline library. Its amount is the lowest of five similarly prepared tail libraries, rather than a subset created for this benchmark. The sample's exact match to the proposed strain reference still needs checking.
limit: The exact sample is Mus musculus, but its strain is not stated. The proposed mouse reference is a same-species proposal; no sequence match is verified.

title: Wheat whole-genome resequencing — Thatcher public input
finding: This ordinary wheat resequencing run adds a large, polyploid crop genome. Both FASTQ ends of one Thatcher sample are included. The primary study reports about 542.5 billion bases and 35× coverage for this sample; this is a real study input, not a subset made to reach a benchmark size. The proposed Renan assembly is from the same species but a different cultivar.
limit: The proposed reference is Renan, not Thatcher; exact read/reference matching remains unverified. Nominal paired 150-base sequencing is documented, but actual FASTQ lengths, qualities, headers and integrity have not been examined.

title: Potato genome assembly — Altus library public input
finding: This PCR-free Altus library adds a tetraploid crop-assembly example. The input is one complete library with a documented 470-base insert. The 470 bases describe the full DNA insert sequenced from both ends, not the length of either read or just the gap between them. Other insert sizes and linked-read preparations are separate libraries.
limit: This is one named PCR-free library, not the entire cultivar assembly dataset. The 470 bp figure is insert size, not read length or verified per-copy depth.

title: Shrimp genome sequencing public input
finding: This run adds a marine invertebrate used in aquaculture breeding research. It gives the collection an animal genome and reference beyond human, mouse and livestock. Its amount is close to the middle of ten comparable runs in the source study.
limit: Raw reference-size ratios are not mapped coverage. The precise whole-sample allocation remains a later preparation check.

title: Chicken genome sequencing public input
finding: This input covers poultry genome resequencing, supported by the breeding-use survey. It is drawn from a substantial study of laying hens. Its amount falls within the middle 80% of the study's reported run amounts.
limit: One applied cohort supports the selected example; it is not a national or global poultry production distribution.

title: Human raw PacBio CLR reads public input
finding: This HG002 library adds raw PacBio CLR reads alongside HiFi consensus reads. The exact library is labelled HG002-CLR. Its supplied quality values and archive format are kept as deposited; they are not assumed to describe native qualities or every raw PacBio file.
limit: Raw pass yield must not be compared directly with HiFi consensus yield or usable coverage. Constant supplied qualities and their archive representation remain explicit.

title: Plant nanopore genome assembly public input
finding: This Arabidopsis Col-0 input adds plant nuclear-genome assembly reads from nanopore sequencing. It is the complete submitted pass-read output of one named run. Fail reads and alternative basecalls are separate representations, not missing pieces of this chosen file.
limit: The chosen PASS output excludes fail reads. Exact basecaller settings are not established, and no whole-flow-cell or whole-file property claim is made.

title: Plant PacBio HiFi genome assembly public input
finding: This Arabidopsis Col-0 readset adds plant HiFi consensus sequencing. The paper's accession, AT_HiFi library name and reported amount agree with the archive record. That documentation establishes the method; the archive filename containing _subreads does not establish it by itself.
limit: Documentary HiFi identity does not establish a particular quality alphabet or whole-file accuracy. The archive filename alone is not processing proof; no new prefix was examined.

title: Human RNA sequencing — MGI public input
finding: This input represents ordinary human RNA sequencing on MGI short-read instruments. It complements the human genomic inputs and the Illumina expression library. Its amount is close to the middle of eight runs in its source study.
limit: Do not compare archive raw read counts directly with an aligned-read standard without resolving the count convention.

title: Plant RNA sequencing public input
finding: This wild-type Arabidopsis Col-0 replicate represents bulk plant RNA sequencing. It is one named expression library, with an amount within the range of fourteen RNA outputs in the source study. The comparison supports this example, not a universal production requirement.
limit: The source describes trimming for analysis; that does not prove the deposited FASTQ was trimmed or untouched. The proposed genomic reference needs an appropriate annotation only for modes that use it.

title: Human small-RNA sequencing public input
finding: This biological replicate represents small-RNA sequencing. Short RNA molecules make it a naturally small input; the inspected reads vary from 18 to 44 bases. The library's read and base totals fit the source study. Its biological target does not establish which trimming steps were applied before deposition.
limit: The exact archive description identifies a size-selected short-RNA library, but does not establish computational trimming before deposition. Saved prefix lengths are not whole-file distributions. No universal read-count threshold or untouched-instrument-output requirement is applied.

title: Human RNA sequencing — Illumina public input
finding: This input represents a conventional Illumina human expression library. It complements the MGI and newer short-read RNA inputs. Its amount is close to the middle of twelve comparable runs in the source study.
limit: The broad RNA archive includes several library designs. Its raw volume supports plausibility, not compliance with a processed/aligned-read standard.

title: Single-end RNA sequencing — Element AVITI public input
finding: This AVITI library adds a commercially deployed short-read technology in its documented single-end RNA configuration. It should be tested as supplied, rather than judged against a paired-end library. Its amount is close to the middle of eighteen source-study runs.
limit: This supports a public research input. Chemistry-specific quality distributions are still unexamined.

title: Nanopore transcript sequencing public input
finding: This input adds nanopore reads from a transcript-derived library, alongside nanopore genomic reads. The source documents a full-length library; that describes the intended sampling, not a guarantee that every deposited read is long or complete. Its read count is comparable to the study's library amounts.
limit: This is same-study scale support, not a general long-RNA production norm. It is not direct RNA, and raw mean length is not comparable with the paper’s filtered/aligned mean.

title: One mouse Smart-seq2 cell public input
finding: This mouse bladder cell adds transcript-wide single-cell RNA sequencing alongside the 3-prime CITE libraries. Smart-seq2 samples across transcripts; it does not make every read span a whole transcript. Both ends of one SRA run are included, with an amount within the middle half of 660 annotated cells.
limit: The full official filename manifest lists one run and two original FASTQ names for this exact well/plate/donor identity. Source label C1 is undefined; no additional part is listed. Completeness is at the deposited-FASTQ boundary, not all instrument/index, aligned-BAM or count-matrix assets. The author annotation does not certify the exact pre-upload processing stage. Archive descriptors specify nominal 100/100-base application reads; actual file properties remain unpreviewed.

title: CITE antibody tags public input
finding: These antibody-derived tag reads complement the mRNA input in Data 31 and sample-tag input in Data 32 from the same CITE experiment. The selected input is one complete paired ADT run, with both ends. Tags carry a different kind of information from transcript reads; the three components are not replicate copies.
limit: This is one archive run, not every output of the component experiment. Recovery targets are not measured recovered-cell counts; exact pre-upload processing and whole-file properties remain unverified.

title: CITE mRNA reads public input
finding: These mRNA reads provide the transcript component of the same CITE experiment as the antibody-tag input in Data 30 and sample-tag input in Data 32. Both FASTQ ends of one complete paired run are included. The tag libraries cannot substitute for this expression library.
limit: This is one archive run, not every output of the component experiment. Recovery targets are not measured recovered-cell counts; exact pre-upload processing and whole-file properties remain unverified.

title: CITE sample tags public input
finding: These sample-tag reads provide the sample-identification component of the same CITE experiment as Data 30 and Data 31. Both ends of one complete paired HTO run are included. It is a naturally small tag input; a tag definition may help interpretation or custom reference matching, but generic lossless compression does not require one.
limit: This is one archive run, not every output of the component experiment. Recovery targets are not measured recovered-cell counts; exact pre-upload processing and whole-file properties remain unverified.

title: Spatial transcript sequencing — Stereo-seq public input
finding: This run adds spatial transcript sequencing, where barcode and transcript reads serve different roles and can have different lengths. The complete named run is large because it is a real spatial input. Its capture area and cell/bin depths are unknown; neither should be inferred from file size.
limit: Capture area and observed cell/bin depths remain unknown. Only three of twelve source-study metadata totals are positive, limiting the amount comparison. Masks and coordinates are interpretation assets, not prerequisites for compression of the supplied reads.

title: Bulk ATAC sequencing public input
finding: This K562 library represents a conventional paired bulk-ATAC replicate. It samples accessible chromatin rather than genome-wide DNA or RNA. Its amount is close to the middle of 32 study runs, although total bases do not establish the number of useful, distinct fragments.
limit: The source establishes a bulk ATAC library, not usable unique-fragment counts or an analysis-pipeline pass. The human reference does not prove K562-specific sequence matching.

title: Rice ChIP sequencing public input
finding: This rice library adds ChIP sequencing, which samples protein-associated chromatin. ATAC and CUT&RUN use different preparations and do not replace it. Its amount is close to the middle of eleven comparable runs in the study.
limit: Raw pairs do not establish aligned, unique or target-specific fragment yield.

title: Human CUT&RUN sequencing public input
finding: This run adds CUT&RUN, documented by its exact experiment even though the archive uses the broad OTHER label. It complements ATAC and ChIP inputs. Its amount falls within the middle 80% of thirty comparable study runs.
limit: Normalization-reference composition and processed/usable depth remain unknown. Do not treat this raw total as a pipeline acceptance result.

title: Yeast Hi-C sequencing public input
finding: This yeast library adds proximity-ligation reads used to study contacts between genome regions. Its compact eukaryotic reference also differs from the large animal and plant references. Its amount lies within both the source-study range and the wider yeast Hi-C comparison.
limit: This supports a yeast research run, not a universal Hi-C target. Valid contacts and intended spatial resolution remain separate from raw volume.

title: Human accessibility sequencing — Ultima public input
finding: This Ultima input adds a deployed sequencing technology in an accessibility assay. The supplied single-read, variable-length format differs from the conventional paired ATAC input. Its amount is within the middle 80% of the 248-run source study.
limit: Do not apply Illumina paired-read or pipeline-pass rules directly. Raw total and the saved prefix do not establish whole-file properties.

title: Rice bisulfite sequencing public input
finding: This rice library adds bisulfite sequencing, whose preparation changes the sequence letters being stored. Ordinary genome sequencing or capture does not supply the same condition. Its amount is comparable to its source study and the wider rice bisulfite examples.
limit: No claim of mapped cytosine coverage, conversion efficiency or compression benefit follows from raw totals.

title: Fungal ITS community markers public input
finding: This soil-root fungal library adds ITS marker sequencing on MiSeq. Both submitted read ends of FL_fungi_1 are included. Its amount is close to the middle of twelve ITS libraries from the same study. Those fungal libraries are compared separately from the study's bacterial 16S libraries.
limit: The exact ITS subregion and pre-upload trimming/filtering stage remain unspecified. Submitted Original status identifies source objects, not untouched instrument reads. A processed but meaningful FASTQ remains eligible; a single tomato or fungal genome would not define this community reference.

title: Bacterial 16S community markers public input
finding: This soil-root bacterial library adds classic 16S community-marker sequencing. Both read ends of SH_bacteria_1 are included. Its amount is close to the middle of twelve bacterial libraries from the study; fungal ITS is a different target and does not replace this input.
limit: The exact 16S subregion and pre-upload processing stage remain unspecified. Neither merging nor untouched raw output is inferred from the file metadata; no single-genome community reference is assumed.

title: Viral amplicon sequencing public input
finding: This specimen-level viral amplicon run adds targeted sequencing of a small genome. Its amount is close to the middle of 58 comparable specimen outputs. A human whole-genome-sized delivery would not represent this task.
limit: This is a plausible specimen-scale targeted input. Target scheme, breadth and usable depth have not been checked.

title: Freshwater environmental-DNA markers public input
finding: This input adds aquatic environmental-DNA marker sequencing. The library is associated with filter ITD20, extraction A and marker set VENE from Lugano. Both archive read ends are included. It is a sample/marker output, not an entire sequencing pool; the exact upstream filtering and barcode-splitting stage is unknown.
limit: The precise upstream demultiplexing and filtering boundary remains unresolved. The author workflow manifest/sample sheet describes an older 2019 run set and does not list the selected accessions; it cannot establish these files’ exact deposited stage. Full-file integrity and pairing remain unverified.

title: Tuberculosis bacterial isolate public input
finding: This input adds a compact bacterial genome beyond E. coli and an inspected trimmed-read format. Its compressed size is below one GB, yet its reported bases are substantial relative to the reference. It lies somewhat above the source study's upper decile, rather than being an ordinary median example.
limit: Raw volume is not usable coverage. Exact sample-strain/reference agreement remains unverified.

title: E. coli bacterial isolate public input
finding: This named MG1655 strain provides a classic bacterial-isolate input with a compact reference. The paired run's amount is close to both its source-study median and the broader E. coli comparison. Exact sample/reference agreement and usable mapped coverage still need checking.
limit: This supports a standard isolate input. Full-file integrity and actual sample/reference sequence agreement remain later checks.

title: Yeast whole-genome sequencing public input
finding: This input adds a compact eukaryotic microbial genome alongside bacterial isolates. Genome sequencing also differs from the yeast Hi-C preparation. Its amount is toward the upper end of its study, making it a high-yield research example rather than a claimed universal norm.
limit: Its ploidy/LOH study purpose is explicit. Do not claim all yeast production normally uses this depth or convert haploid-reference ratios into per-copy coverage.

title: Long-read mock community public input
finding: This run adds long reads from a known mixture of genomes. It differs from single-organism genome sequencing and short community-marker libraries. The source explicitly describes ultra-deep sequencing of a mock community, so its amount belongs to that research purpose.
limit: This represents a real mock/community research input, not an ordinary soil or clinical metagenome depth. The deliberate composition and current basecalling vintage must stay visible.

title: Fermentation community RNA public input
finding: This paired library represents RNA sequencing of a cereal-fermentation community at one named timepoint. Its amount lies within five documented timepoints. It adds a mixed-community RNA task, rather than treating all metagenomic inputs as DNA sequencing.
limit: The source identifies community RNA from a fermentation timepoint, but untouched instrument-output status is not certified. Community composition and a fixed transcript-reference set remain unverified.

title: Soil shotgun community DNA public input
finding: This input represents environmental shotgun DNA sequencing. It complements the gut and food mixtures and the targeted soil-marker inputs. Its amount is close to the middle of eight study runs and consistent with the wider soil comparison.
limit: Community complexity and organism proportions are not measured by these totals. No single-genome coverage is assigned.

title: Gut shotgun community DNA public input
finding: This input represents ordinary human-gut shotgun DNA sequencing. It provides a host-associated community alongside soil and food mixtures. Its amount fits both its source study and the wider gut-study comparison.
limit: The declared run amount and source-study context support this gut shotgun example. Full biological-sample allocation and whole-file properties remain unverified.

title: Honey shotgun community DNA public input
finding: This honey-derived run adds food-associated shotgun DNA sequencing. It is a complete paired run with an amount within the source study's 63-run range. The mixed reference setting differs from pure crop genomes and bacterial isolates; the actual ingredient/community proportions are not established.
limit: This supports a per-product research run. It does not establish general food-industry delivery norms or measured community composition.

limit: ENA generated the listed FASTQs from submitted CRAM; they are not certified untouched instrument files. The exact CHO derivative and agreement with the proposed reference remain unknown. The files and their order, lengths, qualities and integrity have not been examined.
